quiz.0.question: Before opening a Barolo stored horizontally for 20 years, what is the single most important preparation step?
quiz.0.options.0: Chill it in the refrigerator for 30 minutes
quiz.0.options.1: Stand the bottle upright for 24–48 hours to allow sediment to settle to the bottom
quiz.0.options.2: Immediately decant as soon as you remove it from storage
quiz.0.options.3: Warm the bottle in warm water
quiz.0.explanation: Old wines stored horizontally accumulate sediment against the side of the bottle. Standing the bottle upright for 24–48 hours allows sediment to fall to the bottom — making careful decanting without disturbing the sediment possible.
quiz.1.question: Why is using an Ah-So (twin-prong cork puller) strongly recommended for old wines?
quiz.1.options.1: An old, fragile cork may crumble when a screw is inserted — the Ah-So grips both sides of the cork without penetrating it, allowing extraction intact
quiz.1.options.2: It prevents the wine from oxidising
quiz.1.options.3: It is the only tool that fits old bottle sizes
quiz.1.explanation: After 20+ years, natural corks become brittle and compressed. A traditional cork screw risks piercing the centre and causing it to crumble into the wine. The Ah-So's twin prongs slide down the sides of the cork, gripping it without damage.
quiz.2.question: Regarding aged wine 'decanting' vs 'aeration' — which statement is correct?
quiz.2.options.0: All old wines should be aerated for 3+ hours
quiz.2.options.1: Old wines are decanted gently to remove sediment — NOT to add oxygen. Aeration should be brief (30 minutes maximum) as old wines fade quickly when exposed to air
quiz.2.options.2: Old wines do not need decanting at all
quiz.2.options.3: Double decanting (back and forth) is recommended for all old wines
quiz.2.explanation: Old wines are decanted for one reason only: sediment separation. They do NOT benefit from prolonged aeration — unlike young tannic wines, old wines can fade rapidly when exposed to oxygen. Serve soon after decanting.
quiz.3.question: Which glass shape is most suitable for drinking aged Nebbiolo (old Barolo)?
quiz.3.options.1: A large Burgundy-style balloon glass — wide bowl to concentrate aromas, with a slight taper
quiz.3.explanation: Aged Nebbiolo requires a large, wide-bowled Burgundy-style glass — the generous surface area encourages the complex, delicate tertiary aromas (tar, roses, dried violets, earth) to develop and concentrate before tasting.
